title: Prescriptions by mail or common carrier under 247 CMR 9.02
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.02(1) a pharmacy and pharmacist may dispense prescription drugs by mail or common carrier in a manner consistent with federal and state laws and regulations. Under 9.02(2) a pharmacy shall ensure that packing, shipping, and transportation processes do not adversely affect the integrity or stability of medications dispensed by mail. Under 9.02(3) a pharmacy shall maintain policies and procedures regarding packing, shipping, transporting, and delivering controlled substances.
exam_relevance: Separates the three sentences of 247 CMR 9.02: a permission conditioned on other law, an integrity and stability duty on the pharmacy, and a policy-and-procedure duty that the regulation states for controlled substances.
common_confusions: Using a common carrier does not move the 9.02(2) integrity and stability duty off the pharmacy.
The written policy-and-procedure duty in 9.02(3) is stated for controlled substances; the regulation does not state a general written-procedure duty for every shipped drug.
The permission in 9.02(1) is conditioned on consistency with federal and state law, so it does not itself authorize a shipment another law forbids.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-17 in the current official PDF of 247 CMR 9.00 on mass.gov (pages dated 12/6/24).
